Assistant Professor

Education
Professional Appointments
Teaching
Teaching load: averaging 158 hours per year over the 2022–2025 period, 65% above the university requirement.
Active:
Atmospheric Remote Sensing (graduate level, 68 hours per semester, 14-20 students)
Covers atmospheric radiative transfer theory, remote sensing of meteorology and atmospheric composition, Bayesian methods, and five hands-on coding labs.
Atmospheric Physics Lab (undergraduate level, 51 hours per semester, 5-9 students)
Includes 12 different experiments on atmospheric measurement techniques, and I designed five of them.
Interdisciplinary Field Course on Extreme Environments of the Tibetan Plateau (undergraduate level, 10 days each summer, 50-60 students)

Working alongside five faculty members from different schools, I help guide 50–60 students through 12 field experiments conducted at extreme altitudes of 3,000 to 4,000 meters on the Tibetan Plateau. I personally designed and now teach three of these experiments. To support this new course, we are co-authoring a textbook (expected April 2027), and I am responsible for 25% of its content.
Past:
General Physics Lab (undergraduate level, 68 hours per semester, 100-150 students, Fall 2022, Spring 2023, Spring 2024)
Frontiers in Atmospheric Sciences (graduate level, 34 hours per semester, 22 students, Fall 2023)
Research Interests

I study methane, hydroxyl radicals, and air pollutants. I aim to understand the mechanistic links among these species and their feedback on the climate system. My approach integrates atmospheric chemistry modeling and remote sensing, with an emphasis on advancing both methodologies.
